es: Address the player as tú, never usted or vosotros.

Use neutral Spanish that reads naturally in both Spain and Latin America: teléfono (not móvil or celular); mantén presionado (never mantén pulsado); escribe / escribir for typing a name or code (never introduce, introducir or ingresa).

A number placeholder with no _one/_other keys ({{amount}}, {{count}}, {{delta}}…) must read for any number: put it after a colon or in parentheses, or after a noun that does not agree with it. E.g. "Sumar {{amount}} a las vidas", "Cartas de Premio tomadas: {{amount}}", "un cambio de vidas ({{delta}})". Never write "(s)" plurals.

Placeholders such as {{shape}}, {{section}}, {{card}} and {{filter}} can be any gender or number. Never make an article or adjective agree with them; rephrase instead ("{{shape}}, ya en uso", "Mínimo de {{filter}}", "una copia más de {{card}}").

The tú imperative often matches the third person (termina, empieza). When a sentence says what the app or game will do, give it a subject or use the future so it cannot read as an order: "Tu partida terminará sin resultado".
Quote labels, names and search text with « »; keep straight quotes only in examples of text the player types or pastes.
Game, format, variant, card type and product names: use exactly the mapping in the terms. Spanish card and rules wording wins over a literal translation (coste, tirar un dado, rival).

Players can be any gender. Never make a pronoun, adjective or participle agree with a person whose gender the app can't know: the user, a player name, a host or an opponent. Avoid lo/él, listo, ganador, eliminado, «primer jugador» and «Ya eres anfitrión»; use «esa persona», a noun («victoria»), a verb («ganó», «juega primero») or an impersonal form («Todo listo»). A generic masculine plural for a group («Listos: 2 de 4») and a role noun with no specific person (anfitrión, invitado) are fine.
fr: Address the player as vous. Instructions use the vous imperative (Touchez, Réessayez). Buttons and menu actions use the infinitive (Enregistrer, Terminer la partie), never a bare noun such as Fin.

Use the publisher's official French term or name whenever one exists, otherwise what French players say. Leave English only where the glossary keeps it, in quoted parser examples, and in app or product names (Pokémon TCG Live, Fabrary, Limitless).

Typography: a narrow no-break space (U+202F) before ; : ! ? and inside « », never a plain space. Quote with « », never straight quotes, including around English parser examples (the text inside stays exactly as written). Use one apostrophe everywhere: ’ (U+2019). Use … as one character.
Sentence case for titles, buttons and labels (Nouvel événement, not Nouvel Événement). Glossary terms that carry a capital keep it (Banc, Pokémon Actif, Récompense, Lore).

Never write (s), (e) or ils/elles shortcuts. When a count placeholder has no plural forms, or a placeholder's gender is unknown, put the label first: « Ajoutées : {{count}} », « Carte retirée : {{card}} ».
A card name ({{card}}) takes feminine agreement, as « la carte » (est bannie, Retirez-la). Keep the same gender for one placeholder across a whole sentence.
Keep buttons, chips and badges about as short as the English. Prefer the plain everyday word to a literal calque.

Players can be any gender. Never make a pronoun, adjective or participle agree with a person whose gender the app can't know: the user, a player name, a host or an opponent. Avoid lui/le/l', éliminé, prêt, connecté, abonné, bloqué, placé, gagnant and vainqueur on them; use a label-first noun (« Victoire : {{name}} », « Blocage : {{name}} »), an invariable form (hors jeu), « cette personne », or make the account or session the subject (« Session ouverte », « Compte : {{email}} »). A generic masculine plural for a group (« Prêts : 2 sur 4 ») and a role noun with no specific person are fine.
hi: Write in Devanagari and address the player as आप. Other players named in a string take honorific plural verbs: {{name}} पहले खेलेंगे, {{name}} प्राइज़ कार्ड लेते हैं.

Write game, format, variant, card type, set, deck product and rules document names in Devanagari the way Indian players say them: मैजिक, पोकेमॉन, कमांडर, क्रिएचर, प्लेनचेस, कॉम्प्रिहेंसिव रूल्स. When an English note says to keep an official name or term, keep that term but write it in Devanagari.

Latin script stays only where a player has to match or type it exactly: Scryve and its plans (Scryve Pro, Foil, Foil Supporter); platform, store and outside service names (Apple, Google Play, App Store, iPhone, Android, Scryfall, Pokémon TCG Live, MTGO); Wi-Fi, QR, ID, AI, URLs and email addresses; abbreviations printed on cards or used by tournament software (HP, DMG, XP, d6, Bo{{bestOf}}, R{{round}}, 2HG, 2v2, OMW, GW, OGW, OOMW, SoS, and W-L-D only as a standings column header); and anything the deck importer reads (card names, section headers such as Main Deck or Sideboard, YYYY-MM-DD).

Everyday register: write UI Hindi the way people talk, not textbook or government Hindi. Where players and Indian apps use the English word, write it in Devanagari (सेव, एडिट, अनडू, शेयर, इनवाइट, मैनेज, सब्सक्रिप्शन, हिस्ट्री, लोकल); elsewhere use plain spoken Hindi (बाकी, देखें, सबसे नया, इंतज़ार, खत्म, चालू). Avoid लंबित, विफल, समीक्षा, नवीनतम, पात्रता, प्रमाणीकरण, प्रतीक्षा, संपादित, सहेजें, पूर्ववत, आमंत्रण, प्रतिद्वंद्वी, नवीनीकरण, प्रबंधित, सक्रिय, स्थानीय, and समाप्त (except for an expired session or invite).
Build each sentence the way a Hindi speaker would say it, not in English clause order. Keep short labels and badges as short as the English; a label that names a thing or a status takes no करें.

Use these words every time: फ़्री for free (never मुफ़्त); नतीजा for a result (never रिज़ल्ट); पुष्टि for confirm (never कन्फ़र्म); आयोजक for the event organizer; चालू for a game in progress; सेटिंग for Settings, the app's or the phone's (never सेटिंग्स or Latin); गोपनीयता नीति for the Privacy Policy, गोपनीयता for privacy; डेक लिस्ट / लिस्ट for a deck's card list (never सूची); मैन्युअल / मैन्युअली; इंपोर्ट; डाइस and रोल करें (never पासा or फेंका); कलर for a Magic card's color, कलरलेस for colorless (color names like सफ़ेद, नीला and player colors stay रंग); लीगल / बैन for format legality (मान्य means valid); निशान for a player's mark (रंग और निशान); खिलाड़ी for player (never प्लेयर); शामिल होना for joining (never जोड़ना, which means to add).
When running text names a screen, tab, heading or button, quote it with “ ” and copy the exact label that screen shows (“सहायता”, “खेलें” टैब).

Spelling: nukta on फ़ and ज़ in English loanwords (लाइफ़, फ़ॉर्मैट, फ़ोकस, फ़्री); never on क, ख, ग, including Urdu-origin words (आखिरी, तारीख, खराब, खत्म). Chandrabindu, never bindu, in एँ endings and words that take it (जाएँ, हटाएँ, हो जाएँगे, पहुँच, जाँचें, यहाँ). ॉ for the English "o" in draw, toss, lobby (ड्रॉ, टॉस, लॉबी); ै for the "a" in damage (डैमेज).

Gender: लाइफ़, सीट, लॉबी, सेटिंग, स्टैंडिंग, हिस्ट्री, लिस्ट, ग्रिड, पावर, भूमिका, चिप, रूलिंग, पेयरिंग and स्कीम are feminine; लाइफ़ पॉइंट, प्राइज़ कार्ड, डैमेज, लोर, गेम, मैच, टर्न, मुलिगन, इवेंट, खाता, डिवाइस, क्लॉक, स्लॉट, इनवाइट, सब्सक्रिप्शन and फ़ीडबैक are masculine.

Players can be any gender. For another player use the honorific plural ({{name}} जीते, पहले खेलेंगे), a ने-construction or a noun (विजेता: {{name}}); never गया/गई, जीता/जीती or रहा/रही on a person. Never write first-person forms with gendered verbs.
Also feminine: प्रोफ़ाइल, रिपोर्ट, एंट्री, रसीद, कतार. Also masculine: बोर्ड, डेक, ड्राफ़्ट, सेशन, यूज़रनेम.
ja: Messages use です/ます. Buttons and labels use plain verbs or nouns.

Use the publisher's Japanese name for every game, format, variant, product and card term (see the glossary). Where no Japanese name exists, write it in katakana, never Latin. Latin stays only for Scryve and its plans (Pro, Foil), other brands and services (Apple, Google Play, Scryfall, Top Deck, Fabrary, Pokémon TCG Live), Wi-Fi, HP, LP, ID, and anything a note marks as parser input.
Pokémon is ポケモン and the card game is ポケモンカードゲーム (short ポケカ). Never write Pokémon in Latin outside the product name Pokémon TCG Live.
Never add さん, 様 or any honorific after a player placeholder ({{name}}, {{taker}}, {{names}}): {{name}}が先攻です.

Punctuation is full-width: 、。「」？！：（）〜. Digits and Latin letters are half-width. Put no space between a placeholder, number or Latin word and Japanese text ({{elapsed}}前に更新, Scryveのサポート). Keep the English · separator, with a space on each side.
Counters: cards 枚, players 人, distinct cards in a deck 種類 (never エントリー or 件), times 回.
Strings that differ only by game (…mtg, …pokemon, …riftbound) share one Japanese pattern and change only the game's noun.
Leave out あなた and あなたの wherever Japanese drops the subject; a "Your X" label is 自分のX or just X.
ko: Statements, descriptions and errors use 합니다체. Instructions end in -하세요, retry included (다시 시도하세요), never -해 주세요. Confirmations end in -할까요?. Questions to the player may end in -나요 or -인가요 (누가 이겼나요?, 누구 턴인가요?); never -입니까, and no other 해요체 (-예요, -이에요, -해요).
Buttons, menu items, labels, headings and screen-reader action names end in a noun phrase or -기 (저장, 계속 스캔, {{name}}님을 선공으로 표시), never -하세요 or a question. Statuses end in -됨 or -중 (확정됨, 등록 중).
A player's name always takes 님, attached with no space ({{name}}님이, {{name}}님의, {{names}}님). Never after Pokémon, card, deck, team or seat names.

After a name or word placeholder use the fallback particles 이(가), 을(를), 은(는), 과(와), (으)로; never (이)가. Never attach a particle to {{code}}, {{value}} or another number or code: put it after a colon or at the end (참가 코드: {{code}}).

Write every game, format, variant, card type, product and game term in Hangul: the publisher's Korean name where one exists, else what Korean players say (see terms). When an English note says to keep an official term, it means the official Korean term, not the English word.

Latin script only for: Scryve, Scryve Pro and Pro, Wi-Fi, HP, FaB, QR, ID, vs, the OMW/OGW tiebreakers, store and platform names (Apple, Google Play, iPhone, Android), English-only product and file names (Pokémon TCG Live, Fabrary, YDK), the English-only Planechase and Archenemy deck names, and anything a note marks as parser input.
Strings that differ only by game (keys ending .mtg, .ygo, .riftbound and so on) share one Korean pattern; only the counter word changes (생명점, 라이프 포인트, 프라이즈, 로어, 점수).
Translate the meaning, not the words: write what a Korean app would say, and keep the English choices intact (an "or" stays a choice, never "and then").
ar: Write Modern Standard Arabic that reads naturally across the Arab world. Prefer phrasing that avoids grammatical gender for the player (nouns, يمكنك); where an imperative is needed, use the masculine singular, the usual UI convention.

Write every game, format, variant, card type and product name in Arabic script, as the glossary lists it (ماجيك، بوكيمون، يوغي يو!، كوماندر، القياسي). Latin stays only for: Scryve and its plans (Scryve Pro, Pro, Scryve Foil; Supporter is داعم), Riftbound and its proper nouns such as domain names (Riot's Arabic pages keep them in Latin), card names, other companies' apps, sites and platforms (Apple, Google Play, iPhone, Android, Pokémon TCG Live, Scryfall, YGOPRODeck, Limitless), Wi-Fi, QR, file formats (YDK, YDKe), dice notation (d6, d20), and parser input that a note says to keep (sample lines, import headings). Where an English note says to keep an English name, still use the Arabic name when the glossary gives one.

Start every string with an Arabic word so the line stays right to left. Put Latin names and name placeholders ({{name}}, {{card}}) after an Arabic noun: تطبيق Scryve مستقل، اشتراك Scryve Pro مرتبط بحساب، البطاقة {{card}} محظورة. When no sentence fits, use "Arabic label: {{name}}" (المتقدّم في نقاط الحياة: {{name}}).

Never put a gendered verb on a named player. In log rows and status lines, use a verbal noun with the player as its agent (رمية {{name}}: {{face}}، انتقال {{name}} إلى {{plane}}، تفعيل {{name}} للمخطط {{scheme}}) or make the thing the subject (تذهب بطاقات الجائزة إلى {{taker}}).

Never type digits. Numbers come only from placeholders; write one and two as words or with the dual. The only exceptions are digits inside an official product name (بلان تشاس ٢٠١٢, in Arabic-Indic digits), dice notation, and parser input.

A number placeholder without plural forms ({{amount}}, {{limit}}, {{used}}, {{length}}, {{wins}}…) must read for any number. Never put an inflecting noun right after it, and never put it before a definite noun. Use a label and colon (المجموعات المتزامنة: {{used}} من {{limit}}، مستمرة: {{count}}), عدد with a plural (عدد اللاعبين: {{count}}، أدخل الرمز (عدد أحرفه {{length}})), or a preposition (إضافة {{step}} إلى {{label}}). Never "{{count}} لاعبين" or "{{length}} من الأحرف".

Plural slots: the counted noun follows the number category, so every slot differs. one: singular with واحد/واحدة and no number (بطاقة واحدة). two: the dual with no number, nominative when it stands alone (بطاقتان، مباراتان، مقعدان، يومان), genitive only after a preposition or verb object (خلال ساعتين، أضف بطاقتين), and without ن before a following noun (بطاقتا جائزة / بطاقتَي جائزة). few (3-10): {{count}} with the plural (بطاقات، مباريات، أيام). many (11-99): {{count}} with the singular and tanween (بطاقةً، دورًا، يومًا). zero and other: {{count}} with the singular (بطاقة). Never copy one form into every slot.
Touch gestures have one verb: tap is اضغط (اضغط على شارة الدور), long press and hold are اضغط مطولًا. Never المس.

Keep each Arabic word to one job: مجموعة is only a deck, الدور only a turn, نسخة only a copy (of a card, or this device's copy of a deck), مباراة only one game, لعبة only a game system (Magic, Pokémon). Use the glossary term for the other meaning (توسعة، هوية، إصدار).

متصل alone means online right now. For Scryve's connected play, attach متصلة only to مباراة or مباريات (لوحة المباراة المتصلة، سجل المباريات المتصلة); connected play: اللعب عبر الأجهزة; offline: دون إنترنت.
A one-word button must be clear on its own. A bare verbal noun that also reads as a thing (وضع = mode، إدخال = input، التمرير = scrolling) needs its object or an imperative: ضعه، تمرير الدور.
No Latin abbreviations and no invented Arabic ones (Bo3, v2, ي for days). Write the words: الأفضل من {{bestOf}}، الإصدار {{version}}. د for minutes is fine in tight labels.

Never put a gendered verb, adjective, participle or pronoun (ـه، ـها، الفائز، البادئ، جاهز، غائب، خارج) on a named, reported or blocked player, a host or an opponent. Use a verbal noun with the player as agent, a label with a colon (الفوز: {{names}}), or name the thing instead (هذا الحساب، الاسم، الاتصال). For the user, avoid second-person past or present verbs (سجّلت، تختبر، تعود); use passive or verbal-noun forms (تم تسجيل خروجك، عند عودة الاتصال). Imperatives stay masculine singular.

life (Magic, Flesh and Blood, or no game.es: vidas. Heading: Vidas. Counted: 1 vida, 20 vidas; ganar/perder vidas; total de vidas. Never "20 de vida".
life (Magic, Flesh and Blood, or no game.fr: points de vie. Heading: Points de vie. Counted: 1 point de vie, 20 points de vie. Never "20 de vie".
life (Magic, Flesh and Blood, or no game.ar: نقاط الحياة everywhere, including logs, controls and team totals (سجل نقاط حياة {{name}}، تغيير في نقاط الحياة، أدوات التحكم بنقاط الحياة، نقاط حياة الفريق). Bare الحياة only as a standalone heading, never inside a phrase, where it reads as a person's life. Counted: نقطة حياة, following the plural rules

Yu-Gi-Oh! Life Points.ja: ライフポイント (LP in tight labels)
Yu-Gi-Oh! Life Points.ar: نقاط الحياة, the same as Magic life (نقاط الحياة النهائية; counted: نقطة حياة). Heading: الحياة. Never LP

deck.es: mazo for Magic, Lorcana, Flesh and Blood, Riftbound and decks in general (con este mazo, Mazo o comandante); Pokémon: baraja (the Pokémon deck section: Baraja); Yu-Gi-Oh!: Deck. Never "deck" outside Yu-Gi-Oh!
deck.fr: deck, masculine (le deck, ce deck; plural decks)
deck.ja: デッキ; take a card out of a deck: 外す (デッキから外す, 外してください), never 削除 or 取り除く; lower a count: 減らす
deck.ko: 덱 (내 덱, 덱 {{count}}개); a deck's card list: 덱 리스트 (short 리스트); 목록 only for other UI lists
deck.ar: مجموعة (مجموعة أوراق when ambiguous). Only for a deck: a printed card set is توسعة, a group of event tables is طاولة جماعية, a deck version is إصدار

Yu-Gi-Oh! deck sections.es: Deck Principal, Deck Extra, Side Deck. A Yu-Gi-Oh! deck is Deck, never mazo.
Yu-Gi-Oh! deck sections.fr: Yu-Gi-Oh! only: Main Deck, Extra Deck, Side Deck (Konami’s French names). A Magic or Riftbound main deck is deck principal (label: Deck principal), never Main Deck.

Yu-Gi-Oh! deck sections.ja: メインデッキ / エクストラデッキ / サイドデッキ
Yu-Gi-Oh! deck sections.ko: 메인 덱 / 엑스트라 덱 / 사이드 덱
Yu-Gi-Oh! deck sections.ar: المجموعة الرئيسية / المجموعة الإضافية / المجموعة الجانبية

Magic sideboard.fr: réserve (la réserve; en réserve; label: Réserve; 15 en réserve). Swapping cards between games: ajuster la réserve. Magic main deck: deck principal. Side Deck and Main Deck are Yu-Gi-Oh! words only. Import headings quoted as parser input (Mainboard, Sideboard) stay as written.
Magic sideboard.hi: साइडबोर्ड (short: साइड; main deck: मेन डेक, short: मेन)
Magic sideboard.ja: サイドボード (counted: サイドボード{{count}}枚)

Pokémon Prize cards, and taking one.es: cartas de Premio, capital P (1 carta de Premio). Take a Prize card: tomar (never coger)
Pokémon Prize cards, and taking one.fr: cartes Récompense (Récompense is capitalized and invariable: 2 cartes Récompense; short form Récompenses). Take a Prize card: récupérer
Pokémon Prize cards, and taking one.hi: प्राइज़ कार्ड (take: लेना; give back: लौटाना)
Pokémon Prize cards, and taking one.ja: サイド (never サイドカード; counted サイド{{count}}枚); take: とる (サイドをとる)
Pokémon Prize cards, and taking one.ko: 프라이즈 (counted 프라이즈 {{count}}장; never 사이드). Take: 프라이즈를 가져오다 / 가져가다

Active Pokémon / Active Spot.hi: ऐक्टिव पोकेमॉन; the spot: ऐक्टिव (ऐक्टिव में लौटता है)
Active Pokémon / Active Spot.ja: バトルポケモン; the spot: バトル場; put a Pokémon into play: 出す (バトル場に出す), never 置く or 配置
Active Pokémon / Active Spot.ko: 배틀 포켓몬 (spot: 배틀 필드, with a space)
Active Pokémon / Active Spot.ar: the Pokémon: البوكيمون النشط; the place on the board: الموضع النشط (يعود إلى الموضع النشط). Placing one: ضع بوكيمون نشطًا, never a bare وضع; none there: بلا بوكيمون نشط

Bench.ja: ベンチ / ベンチポケモン; put one there: ベンチに出す

HP.hi: HP, in Latin script ({{remaining}} HP बचे)
HP.ja: HP, number after: HP{{hp}}, 残りHP{{remaining}}; heal: HPを{{amount}}回復 (never ダメージを回復)
HP.ar: نقاط الصحة; with numbers use a label (نقاط الصحة المتبقية: {{remaining}} من {{hp}}); short unit chip: الصحة. Never HP

damage (Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Magic).es: daño. Counted: 30 de daño (Sumar {{amount}} de daño); short: DÑO, 30 dño; deal: infligir; heal: curar
damage (Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, Magic).ko: Pokémon and Yu-Gi-Oh!: 데미지. Magic: 피해 (counted 피해 3점). Never 대미지.

Lorcana lore.fr: Lore. A counted amount is éclats de Lore (1 éclat de Lore, 20 éclats de Lore).
